posts.author: dave battin
posts.content_md:
when acquiring glass i have found a great source is at your local art store, the type that has a special every week, (here its called Michael's), Its the replacement glass sold for picture frames, located in or near the framing department. it comes cleaned sealed and slightly lighter/weight than the regular 1/8" glass found at the local hardware store. the largest i can get is 16"x20" for @ $5 each, not bad for coming cleaned and ready to cut .................. subbing will be next

![Image](http://members.aol.com/holoart/hologlass.jpg)

I have found it much easier to cut the glass into 4”x16” pieces before subbing.

![Image](http://members.aol.com/holoart/cutglass.jpg)

A simple jig to cut your glass will give you nice consistent cuts every time.

By banking your glass to the stop and placing the proper width spacer on top, simply

bank your glasscutter against the spacer and slice. It’s best to provide a little lubricant

to help the cut a little (I lick the cutter first).

Now that my glass is cut, I'll prep the surface for coating.

This glass is pretty clean already. If you’re unsure, I would soak it in a 20% Clorox Solution (soak over night), and after a quick water wash, soak in the Cascade (dishwasher soap) and water mix (I use a small handful for 2 gallons of water or so) again soak overnight after a slight 

scrubbing action using a plastic scrubby pad.

![Image](http://members.aol.com/holoart/cascade.jpg)

After removal of the glass from the Cascade, I give it a quick dip into clean water

and then a final plunge into what they refer to as (Trisodium Phosphate) substitute. Where I live, they won’t allow the use of the real TSP, as it’s bad for the ground water. Allow to dry by leaning on wall, sitting on a paper towel. 

![Image](http://members.aol.com/holoart/tsp.jpg)

The glass is now ready to be coated, but we must add a few extra items to make things easier later on …………………………

![Image](http://members.aol.com/holoart/coating1.jpg)

posts.author: dave battin
posts.content_md:
Sorry for the interruption as I took a short holiday to the east end of long island...........

So now, let’s proceed where we left off:

I would normally do all the pre-work under my laminar flow booth and not on the dining room table.

![Image](http://members.aol.com/holoart/taping.jpg)

It helps to place your plate (the glass will now be referred to as plate) on some type of pedestal (as shown) or block of wood. (photo A)

Start by placing the plate face down on the pedestal and applying plain old ordinary scotch tape to both long sides of plate, adhere tape directly to the back of the plate, allowing only half of the tape to hang off the sides the entire length of the plate (photo B). I call these gutters. These will allow you to coat your plate up to the very edge without any waste.

Once the gutters are in place, turn your plate face up, and again place on the pedestal.

Now using a short piece of tape slightly longer than the width of your plate, attach it to the top, adhering directly onto the face of the plate, again leaving half the tape to hang off the top (photo C).

Now that the top tape is adhered, we will now apply the “Tab”, a small 1x5 inch piece of paper applied from the back of the plate stuck to the tape along the top. This tab will be used numerous times throughout the operation so be sure its adhered well (photo D).

Your plate should now look like this:

![Image](http://members.aol.com/holoart/tapingclose.jpg)

The next steps will show the coating process.

posts.author: dave battin
posts.content_md:
The paper tab I attached to the top of the plate, will now act as a handle and I can hold it while doing a final cleaning, I lay the glass across my leg and wipe it clean (front only)using a folded paper towel and simple Windex glass cleaner ,always spray on the towel and not the glass! 

With my method of coating i felt to lean is to be constant! The angle of incline is not so important, but its to always repeat the same angle, i achieve this by placing a pen line on the wall and match the top of the plate to it, see the video to help explain. Using the same paper tab again, i scotch tape it to the wall (i use the side glass of my laminar flow booth)and the film is now ready for coating .

a few minuets after coating , the paper tab will now allow you to attach a large paper clip ,and hang your film to dry. By using a lab base and thin rod clamped horizontally, its easy to hang 12 4x5s to dry!

i heat my plate just before coating with as much heat as possible .

(highheat and blow settig)

The blow dryer i use is old and weak! But it has two settings hi/low

heat, at low it is very weak (blowing),and you will see me blowing close to the wet emulsion. Most new blow dryers will be way to powerful for this.

to apply the emulsion i use a simple squirt bottle, very easy to regulate flow, with the current bottle, i can coat three 4x16 plate before i have to recharge the bottle.

the following video should help to make it all very clear ......

first off ,im really glad to get the video to work! it was a little frustrating to say the least! LOL

to try to answer your questions:

i found when coating ,if i did only one coat it was too thin, always producing a blue to green holo,compared to gold from my drawn bar film. In my thinking i know the first coat grabs on to the glass, so why not place another coat right away

(as long as your glass is still warm), it would possibly come out thicker?

well it did and also did a really nice job doing the veiling........

the TSP bath is really a TSP substitute,used to prep surfaces before painting (and claims to be neutral based)..... when the glass is removed from it, it feels sticky/super clean(as if anything would stick to it yet clean as a whistle).

i normally use 10-30-250 mix for DCG .I go a little heavy on the water,

 as i find the water evaporates quickly from recycling the batch (which i filter at every cycle using a funnel and nylon stocking)...

i would think by adjusting the gelatin amount and/or plate angle, this would delta the thickness.The color/thickness is uniform to within a 1/4" of all edges ,as far as the actual thickness, i really don't have the ability to check

it....
